races.name: Ascona Ladies Fuelled By Fashion Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sixtygeesbaby
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner with three wins and five places from 15 starts on similar going; uncontested lead on a flat track at Ffos Las is a major asset, though the P-tagged style fit note signals she is occasionally effective racing off the pace too — here she is squarely in her most natural position.

runners_data.name: Safari Dream
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up specialist who has won on good ground at six furlongs and recorded course form, but a modest uncontested pace from Sixtygeesbaby is the worst possible scenario for a genuine closer needing horses to come back to her; Finley Marsh will need a slice of luck.

runners_data.name: Army Bugler
runners_data.note: Three-year-old stepping up to six furlongs for just the second time having won over five; form figures of 2/6f/GOO suggest the extra furlong suits, and Harry Vigors' 5lb claim could be decisive if he can track the leader closely throughout on this flat track.

runners_data.name: Alkuwarrior
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted three-year-old with hold-up tendencies and a one-win record from 14 starts; Gina Mangan faces a stiff ask if the pace remains moderate, and the move from five to six furlongs at this level has yet to produce a convincing performance over the longer trip.

runners_data.name: Liosa
runners_data.note: Has won and placed prominently at this course and distance on good ground, which is genuinely encouraging form — but in this field she is a front-running type displaced from her natural prominent position, meaning she may race without the lead she needs to show her best; Oliver Carmichael's 7lb claim helps the weight.

runners_data.name: Pull The Rug
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator whose best run of late was a second over six furlongs on good ground, but has yet to win over the trip; mapped to midfield as a redistribution from a crowded rear group, and Robbie Downey must wait for a gap that a controlled pace will make difficult to find.

races.paceDynamic: Sixtygeesbaby is the lone confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should be allowed to dictate a controlled, unchallenged gallop from the front over Ffos Las's straight six furlongs on good ground. The pace is unlikely to be truly searching — a lone leader rarely sets a punishing tempo when unpressured — which typically compresses the field and makes it harder for hold-up horses to generate the momentum they need late. Safari Dream and Alkuwarrior are the genuine hold-up types here, and on a flat track with a modest pace they will need the race to fall apart in front of them to land a telling blow from the rear. This field holds more prominent-type runners than can realistically occupy those forward positions: Liosa and Pull The Rug are natural prominent horses pushed back on the pace map, and Sixtygeesbaby is far more likely to hold the lead unchallenged than any of them are to disrupt her. The shape strongly favours horses who can sit close to a controlled pace and quicken — prominent trackers and races-from-the-front profiles are the primary beneficiaries here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sixtygeesbaby Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sixtygeesbaby breaks cleanly and sets an uncontested, sustainable gallop with no rival applying pressure.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard of the six furlongs, keeps the tempo honest to preserve her energy, and arrives at the final furlong with enough in the tank to repel challengers. Horses with prominent cruising speed who can sit on her girths are best placed to threaten, as the held-up pair face too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Army Bugler tracks Sixtygeesbaby closely throughout and the leader begins to tire inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Army Bugler's step up in trip from five furlongs to six on good ground and his recent placed form suggests he has the profile to sit just off the pace and outlast the leader late. A prominent style on a flat track with a modest pace is exactly the shape he needs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Capitalises On Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves faster than anticipated and the front horses tie up in the final two furlongs, handing the hold-up horses a run through.
scenarios.body: Safari Dream has the course-and-distance winning form and the class to finish powerfully if a gap materialises, with a genuine hold-up style that delivers only when the race genuinely falls apart.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Pace Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If a slow or uneven start causes positional chaos and horses race out of their natural roles throughout.
scenarios.body: This low-probability shape benefits whichever horse best handles the tactical confusion, but with redistributed horses already racing against their natural style the outcome becomes largely unpredictable. Safari Dream's consistent course form gives her marginal resilience in a scrambled race.

watchPoints.text: Sixtygeesbaby is the single pace-controlling force in this race — if she is allowed a clean break and an uncontested lead, watch for whether any rider attempts to go with her early, as that would materially alter the tempo and the race shape.

Army Bugler's starting position and early stride are worth tracking — if Harry Vigors gets him to track Sixtygeesbaby's quarters within the first furlong, the race shape switches from a lone-leader scenario to a contested one.

Liosa and Pull The Rug are both racing out of their natural positions; watch whether either jockey attempts to push forward from the gates to reclaim their preferred ground, which could inject unexpected early pace into what looks a one-paced affair.

Safari Dream and Alkuwarrior will need to be closer than their natural styles suggest by halfway if the pace is controlled — watch their positions at the two-furlong marker as a signal of whether either can produce a meaningful late challenge.

races.name: Ascona Ladies Chic Fashion Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sofian
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has shown a willingness to close from off the pace over 7-8f on good ground, posted a recent second on similar conditions; trainer Nikki Evans has had limited recent action and Kieran O'Neill takes the ride 17 days fresh — best served by a fast early tempo that this race may not provide.

runners_data.name: Searchingtheblues
runners_data.note: Apprentice Rose Dawes (5lb claimer) takes the ride for Mark Usher, who is in fair recent form (1/12 in 14 days); the horse's form string shows modest efforts on standard and soft, with only one place from fifteen runs on similar ground — needs everything to go right.

runners_data.name: Cypriot Diaspora
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner with full control of the pace; has placed twice in her last five starts on good ground over 7-8f and Rod Millman's yard is light on winners in the last fortnight, but the tactical advantage of uncontested lead-setting at 7½f on a flat track is significant.

runners_data.name: Kaleidoscope Eyes
runners_data.note: Recorded a win and two places from six starts on good or good-to-firm ground; by nature a genuine hold-up horse but the surplus of closers in this field means she will race in a midfield cluster rather than from her favoured deep draw — a style-fit compromise that tempers her finishing threat.

runners_data.name: Oviedo
runners_data.note: Won on good ground over 8f last time out (9 days ago, quick return) for the lightly-used Alexandra Dunn yard, but that effort came from a hold-up position and she carries a flagged tendency to fade late; forced into midfield rather than her natural rear berth, her stamina may not extend fully over 7½f at this pace.

runners_data.name: Green Icon
runners_data.note: William Carson's mount has a poor recent sequence (000807) and has struggled badly on good ground at 6-7f in recent starts; tagged as a natural hold-up type displaced into midfield, and two finish-fade flags suggest she needs things to fall perfectly to threaten.

runners_data.name: Ravenglass
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran wearing a hood, showing a consistent if modest profile — four places from his last five on good ground at 6-7f; a genuine closer who will be squeezed into a midfield cluster, but his track-record on this going and distance band (9/15 sim-going, 1W4P) gives him the best closing credentials of the hold-up group if a gap materialises.

races.paceDynamic: Cypriot Diaspora is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 7½f handicap and, with no identified pace rival to pressure her, she is set to dictate at a controlled, sustainable tempo on good ground at Ffos Las. The remainder of the field — Sofian, Searchingtheblues, Kaleidoscope Eyes, Oviedo, Green Icon, and Ravenglass — are all hold-up or come-from-behind types, meaning the early fractions will be set entirely by Cypriot Diaspora with no genuine challenge for the lead. This race shape — a lone leader, moderate pace, and a pack of closers who must produce their effort from a similar position late — classically favours the horse on the front end who can control tempo and build a buffer before the home turn, making a well-judged front-running display the dominant threat. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can meaningfully be separated at the rear; Kaleidoscope Eyes, Green Icon, and Ravenglass all have genuine closing profiles but will be racing in a compressed midfield group rather than from their ideal deep position, which dilutes the effectiveness of their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cypriot Diaspora Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Cypriot Diaspora gets a soft lead, sets a measured pace, and kicks clear before the home straight is reached.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard in comfort, builds an uncontested advantage into the final two furlongs, and the hold-up pack — unable to spread out and facing a compressed run home — cannot reel her in in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Cut Through
scenarios.trigger: If Cypriot Diaspora's pace is slow enough to allow a late burst from a well-positioned closer who finds a clear run.
scenarios.body: A horse tracking mid-division moves with the first serious effort inside the final two furlongs and catches a tiring leader; the compressed midfield group means a clean switch is decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstayed
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is quicker than expected and Cypriot Diaspora's stamina frays in the final furlong of this 7½f trip.
scenarios.body: The leader hits a flat spot inside the final furlong and a horse who has been travelling kindly just behind sweeps past; good ground suits a horse with a turn-of-foot.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Contest
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed field produces interference, a false pace, or multiple horses fail to find clear daylight in the straight.
scenarios.body: No horse can produce a decisive effort cleanly, the race is messy and the result hinges on a fortunate run through; a horse with low draw or wide berth benefits.

watchPoints.text: Cypriot Diaspora's ability to establish an uncontested lead within the first furlong is the single most important event in this race — if she slots in front unchallenged by the quarter-mile mark, she controls the outcome.

Kaleidoscope Eyes, Green Icon, and Ravenglass will all be hunting the same strip of ground in the straight — watch for crowding, checks, or one horse being forced wide while another gets the clean run.
Oviedo returns just nine days after her last run; monitor paddock behaviour and early race demeanour, as the quick turnaround combined with a fade-flag could mean she empties out before the line.

Searchingtheblues is equipped with headgear (p) and has placed on her only comparable going run; Rose Dawes claims 5lb, which is meaningful at these low weights — watch whether the claimer can position her closer than her natural style suggests.
Green Icon has finished in double figures in four of her last five starts on good ground at this trip — if she is taken off her feet early, her chance is likely gone before halfway.

races.name: Ascona Ladies In Lace Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Korbut
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's mare has run six consecutive placed efforts, all at 6-7f on Standard/Soft, and steps onto Good turf for the first time — her style=Lead profile suits this perfectly with zero pace rivals to challenge her; Luke Morris, a Prescott staple, will maximise the uncontested lead, though the going switch from Standard is the only mild query.|

runners_data.name: Likeness
runners_data.note: Jack Channon returns this hold-up filly after a 138-day absence with only one trainer run in the past 14 days (1 from 15), and her best effort was a second over 7f on Standard ground; she has a proven similar-going record of 1W/1P from 7f, but the small field and controlled pace are structurally against her late-running style, meaning she requires a pace collapse she is unlikely to get here.|

runners_data.name: Reader
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning's lightly-raced filly has placed twice on Good ground and twice at 6f, now tackling 7½f for the first time, which may stretch her stamina slightly; Jack Doughty has just one trainer run in six days and will likely track Korbut in second throughout, giving her a prominent position that could see her closest at the line if Korbut weakens, though the step up in trip is an unknown.|

races.paceDynamic: Korbut is the sole confirmed front-runner in a three-horse field and will lead from the outset on Good turf over 7½f at Ffos Las, facing zero pace pressure from Reader (prominent) or Likeness (hold-up). With no rival willing or able to contest the early lead, Korbut will dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop, setting her own fractions and conserving energy for the closing stages. Likeness will be anchored off the pace by George Bass, while Reader is likely to track a comfortable second, leaving Korbut with a clear tactical advantage throughout. This race shape strongly favours the front-running profile — an uncontested leader on Good ground over a distance she has run repeatedly is handed the ideal opportunity to control tempo and repel challengers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Korbut Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Korbut dictates an uncontested, controlled pace and the field fails to close on the turn.
scenarios.body: Korbut sets fractions entirely to her liking, hits the home straight with petrol in the tank, and her rivals are left with too much ground to make up against a fresher front-runner; her consistent form of placed efforts at this trip on Standard and this first time on Good makes her the one to beat. Prominent runners tracking comfortably in second have the best chance of running her down, but the hold-up horse Likeness will need an unlikely collapse from the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Reader Tracks and Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Reader sits a length off Korbut throughout and produces a sustained challenge entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Reader's two placings on Good ground and the step back from 8f to a sharper 6f in past form suggests she handles this surface and could benefit from a controlled pace that suits a closer-tracking style; Jack Doughty can position her ideally in second without burning energy. A well-timed challenge at the two-furlong pole could catch a front-runner who has over-committed on the front end.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Likeness Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the closing stages and Likeness produces a strong late run from well off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Likeness has shown ability in similar company with a win at 7f on Standard ground, and a 138-day break with Jack Channon's yard could mean she returns sharpened; however, a genuine hold-up horse in a three-runner field faces a structurally poor scenario where the pace may be too steady to open gaps. George Bass will need a slow early pace to be fully wound up and a faltering Korbut to make this viable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Finish, All Beaten
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at an unusually slow overall tempo causing a bunch finish with all three riders misjudging.
scenarios.body: Three runners with no pace conflict could produce a dawdle that turns the final two furlongs into a sprint, nullifying any positional advantage and making the result nearly impossible to predict on form; topspeed figures and freshness become the only differentiator. This scenario is unlikely given Sir Mark Prescott's trademark efficiency and Korbut's established front-running role, but is not impossible in a thin maiden field.

watchPoints.text: Korbut's going switch from Standard/Soft to Good is the one genuine unknown — watch the market move and pre-race demeanour to gauge whether Prescott has flagged any concern about the surface.

Likeness's 138-day absence means fitness is unproven on return; if she is short of her peak, the hold-up style in a three-runner controlled-pace race is the worst possible combination and she may find herself permanently detached.
Reader's first attempt at 7½f after runs exclusively at 6f is an untested stamina query — if she over-commits tracking Korbut early, she may flatten out in the final furlong rather than challenging.

With only three runners, any early hesitation at the start or crowding in the initial strides could reshape positions instantly — watch for Reader and Korbut to establish their roles within the first two furlongs as this will define the entire race shape.

races.name: Ascona Ladies Fashion And Style Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Medyg
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose recent form figures of 9-8-9 are deeply unpromising; trainer Smyth-Osbourne has no winners from six 14-day runners, sim-going record shows no wins or places, and the step up beyond 6f has yet to yield improvement — hard to make a case here.

runners_data.name: Willowinghurn
runners_data.note: True hold-up runner with an excellent sim-going record of 4 places from 11 runs on Good, consistently competitive at 7-8f; trainer O'Meara is in strong form (8/52 14-day), only 9 days since last run which is fine for this type, and she is the most solid form option in the chasing pack.

runners_data.name: Lady Fizz
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in the finish, which is a significant concern at 7½f; sim-going record of just 1 run from 4 on Good is thin, and the pattern of drifting back through the field late makes her vulnerable in any scenario that needs a decisive closing kick.

runners_data.name: Gal
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who has won on Good ground and carries a STYLE_FIT flag having been redistributed to midfield — she will likely be further back than ideal; the fades-in-finish tag is a real concern at this trip, though her Good-ground win shows ability when conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Iconic Dawn
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who has placed three times from seven sim-going starts without winning; Gina Mangan takes the ride for Hughie Morrison whose 14-day record (1/6) is modest, and the tongue-tie suggests some behavioural management — capable of hitting the frame if she secures a clean passage.

runners_data.name: Golden Mabel
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type pushed into the mapped midfield by the redistribution — her actual race position will be further back than the map suggests, compounding a record of no wins and no places on Good; headgear (hood) noted but the form figures of 5-7-8-6-6-8 do not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Diamond Ali
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and the key pace influence in this race; she has a recent win (1/8f/SOF) and Good-ground form, wears a peg, and William Carson's experience in getting her to relax in front is crucial — her STYLE_FIT flag reflects that her natural P style aligns perfectly with the map position she will actually get.

runners_data.name: Cougar Force
runners_data.note: A natural closer redistributed to midfield, meaning her actual running position will be deeper than the map shows; best form has come at 5-6f and the step up to 7½f looks a question, despite placing twice on Good — 87 days off the track is another flag worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Follow My Heart
runners_data.note: Rod Millman runner placed four times from eight Good-ground starts but never won; a true hold-up type mapped to midfield due to redistribution — she will race further back than ideal — and the trainer's 14-day record (0/19) is poor, making this a tough ask at 7½f.

runners_data.name: Arvana Belle
runners_data.note: Millman's second runner; notably has the best sim-going record in the field (10 from 12 starts, one win, three places on Good) and has finished third twice at 7f on Good — the redistribution maps her to midfield but her genuine position will be further back, so she needs the race to truly set up for closers.

runners_data.name: Independent Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly placed to midfield on the map but likely to race deeper; best form has come at 5-6f and the jump to 7½f looks a stretch — Independent Angel has been tailed off twice recently and the Williamson yard's modest 14-day numbers (1/8) do not encourage.

runners_data.name: Kaiko
runners_data.note: Very lightly raced (form: 5-9-6) with a slim sim-going sample of one run from three on Good; Wintle trainer has had a 14-day winner (1/5) but Kaiko is the least exposed runner in the field and, while that cuts both ways, the form in the book does not point to an imminent breakthrough at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Diamond Ali is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a field of 12 at 7½f on Good ground at Ffos Las, she is likely to bowl along at a comfortable, controlled tempo from the outset — a sustainable gallop that keeps her reserves intact for the finish. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly hold-up in style: Gal, Golden Mabel, Cougar Force, Follow My Heart, Arvana Belle, Independent Angel and Kaiko are all true closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would naturally choose, compressing the midfield and reducing the tactical gaps available to genuine late finishers. This redistribution effect means the rear of the field is far less populated than it appears — horses nominally shown in midfield are in reality racing out of their preferred role, and any scenario that depends on a sweeping late challenge is less likely to materialise cleanly. With Diamond Ali dictating an uncontested, metronomic pace and the hold-up brigade bottled up behind her, the race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can race prominently or at worst in the first half of the field and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — a race for the patient stalker rather than the deep closer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Diamond Ali Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Ali is allowed to stride into a comfortable lead unchallenged and sets an honest but not brutal tempo.
scenarios.body: Diamond Ali settles into her rhythm on the front end and, with no rival willing or able to apply sustained pressure, rations her effort perfectly around the Ffos Las track before holding on through the final furlong; at 7½f on Good ground her stamina profile is sufficient to last the trip at this pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that Diamond Ali ties up in the last two furlongs, opening the door for a closing burst.
scenarios.body: The field concertinas turning for home and a horse who has managed to secure a better-than-expected position in the bunched midfield gets a clear run and finishes fastest of all; Willowinghurn, who has strong Good-ground form at this trip, and Gal, a proven winner on Good, are best placed to capitalise if Diamond Ali cries enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Diamond Ali just off the pace and kicks decisively when Diamond Ali's advantage narrows in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: A prominent or close-tracking ride at this trip on Good ground suits a horse with enough tactical speed to accelerate when the leader is caught, rather than relying on a pure late burst from off the bridle; Arvana Belle's recent Good-ground form at 7f and Iconic Dawn's profile make them candidates if they secure a forward enough pitch.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Profit
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Ali goes off too hard early and the pace collapses dramatically, gifting late runners an unusually strong finish.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires conditions that are not presently indicated — Diamond Ali is a confirmed pacemaker rather than a front-running bolter — so it is low probability; if it does occur, the deepest-lying true closers such as Medyg and Lady Fizz would benefit, though both carry significant form doubts at this trip.

watchPoints.text: Diamond Ali (William Carson) — watch whether she is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged from the outset; if she gets a soft lead she could prove very difficult to reel in over 7½f on this Good surface.

Gal (Luke Morris) — flagged as fading in the finish and redistributed deeper than her natural position; watch where Morris settles her in running — if she ends up in the rear third she may not get competitive with her style-fit concern at this trip.

Willowinghurn (Joe Leavy) — the most consistent hold-up performer on Good ground in this field, only nine days since last run; watch whether Leavy can manoeuvre her into a position just behind the leaders to avoid being blocked in the bunched midfield.

Cougar Force (George Bass) — 87 days off the track is worth monitoring in the pre-race paddock; if she looks in peak condition she is capable on Good ground at shorter trips, but this distance and absence combined merit caution.

The redistribution effect — with seven or more true hold-up types all seeking to race further back than the map allows, watch for a compacted, traffic-heavy situation in the final three furlongs where horses become blocked behind rivals, particularly affecting Gal, Golden Mabel and Independent Angel.

races.name: Ascona Fabulous Ladies Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: A Rose Adaay
runners_data.note: Consistently placed at 8f on Good ground (three places from six recent starts) but all form is at shorter than today's 1m2f, and as a natural hold-up type in a field dominated by backmarkers she is unlikely to get a clean position — the step up in trip on this flat track is the key unknown for her chance.

runners_data.name: Charencey
runners_data.note: Strong recent form at exactly this trip — two consecutive placed efforts at 12f and 10f on Good ground — and wears a tongue-tie today; a genuine hold-up horse who will struggle to get her natural backmarker berth in this field, but Ian Williams's yard is in decent form and she warrants respect if she finds a run.

runners_data.name: City Escape
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old who has posted five consecutive finishes of 5th or 6th at 10f on similar ground, and wears eye-shields; her naturally deep hold-up style is the hardest to accommodate in this pace shape and her recent consistency in midfield makes her reliable at best rather than a genuine winner.

runners_data.name: Gert Lush
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts from four 2024 starts at 9-10f on Good, trained by Roger Teal who has a 14-day strike rate of 1/11 — she races in hold-up style but has shown a willingness to travel into contention, making her better placed than true closers if the pace is slow, and today's 12f trip is a slight stretch.

runners_data.name: King Of The Dance
runners_data.note: Wearing a bit today after some erratic running (including an unseated), this 7yo has most of his placed form over 7-8f rather than today's 1m2f, and his natural backmarker style combined with the trip extension makes him a difficult fit — Donagh Murphy claims 7lb but the profile doesn't suit this race shape.

runners_data.name: Prophet Squeeze
runners_data.note: An 8yo wearing a hood, with no wins and no places from five recent starts on Good going and a refused-to-race in his form string — his true hold-up profile is the deepest in the field and the lack of a genuine pace makes this almost impossible for him to run his race.

runners_data.name: Racing Demon
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has a four-placing streak from recent runs showing genuine consistency, with his best form at 8-10f; Luke Morris is an experienced handler of pace scenarios and if Racing Demon can place himself closer than his natural style allows, his finishing effort may be better than his hold-up tag suggests.

runners_data.name: Strong Man Tom
runners_data.note: A 4yo flagged for fading in the finish, with all four recent efforts showing poor finishing positions and a form string reading 6609 — the step to 1m2f and the slow pace both work against him, and wearing a tongue-piece and pad he has very little to recommend him in this shape.

runners_data.name: Typeface
runners_data.note: Two wins from recent form (shown in a 7-6433 string suggesting solid mid-race positions), trained alongside Charencey by Ian Williams, and wears a hood today; his 10f form on Good is the most consistently strong here and he profiles as one of the likelier winners if he can travel close enough to the modest pace set by Lapidarist.

runners_data.name: Elora Prince
runners_data.note: The lightest weight in the field at 128lbs as a 3yo, with six consecutive finishes of 4th to 9th and all recent form at 8-10f on Good — a genuine hold-up operator who is very unlikely to get her natural deep position in this congested field, and the 12f trip represents a stretch given her juvenile record.

runners_data.name: Lapidarist
runners_data.note: Redistributed to the lead as the only identifiable pace-setter — actually a natural prominent/hold-up type for David Simcock — and carries 128lbs as a 3yo; her STYLE_FIT score of 0.80 reflects the discomfort of being asked to front-run, but the complete absence of natural leaders means she will likely find herself alone in front whether she wants to be or not.

races.paceDynamic: Lapidarist is the sole identified pace-setter in this 11-runner 1m2f contest at Ffos Las, redistributed to the lead from a prominent tag — meaning this race is unlikely to be run at a genuinely hot gallop, and the pace will be controlled and sustainable on Good ground. With one horse setting a modest tempo unchallenged, the race is likely to develop into a slowly-run, bunched affair where runners settle through the middle stages before a stamina-test in the closing two furlongs. This pace shape classically advantages hold-up horses who can produce a sustained late run — however, the critical complication here is that this field is almost entirely composed of hold-up types, meaning genuine late-closers will face a congested final furlong with nowhere to go if the pace is slow. The race shape therefore most favours runners who can travel prominently just off the lazy early pace, and then quicken — horses like Typeface, Gert Lush, and Racing Demon, who have shown an ability to place themselves and finish through the field, are better suited than pure late-closers who depend on a strong pace to pull them into contention. Several runners including Charencey, City Escape, Elora Prince, and King Of The Dance are genuine hold-up types who cannot all get their natural backmarker position; Charencey and Racing Demon, given their recent form at this trip, are most likely to secure a tactically useful position just off the modest pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lapidarist Controls, Hold-Up Poaches
scenarios.trigger: If Lapidarist sets a steady, uncontested lead and the hold-up pack settles in behind without a midrace injection of pace.
scenarios.body: Lapidarist dictates a modest tempo around Ffos Las's flat circuit, and those able to travel close enough to the pace through the middle stages pounce in the final two furlongs before the true backmarkers can reel them in. Typeface and Gert Lush, both capable of racing closer than their hold-up tag suggests and with good form at this trip on Good ground, are the profiles best placed to benefit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Congested Finish, Closers Squeeze Through
scenarios.trigger: If the slow early pace compresses the field and a late sprint develops, allowing the freshest hold-up horse to thread through.
scenarios.body: With a modest gallop set by Lapidarist, the entire pack is bunched approaching the final bend, and the race becomes a sprint from two furlongs out — rewarding the horse with the clearest run and the freshest legs late on. Racing Demon and Charencey, both with strong recent form at 10-12f on Good going, carry the profile to capitalise if gaps appear in a tight finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lapidarist Front-Runs Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Lapidarist's sustainable lead proves too comfortable to reel in and the hold-up pack never gets into gear in time.
scenarios.body: A controlled, uncontested lead on Good ground over 1m2f at Ffos Las is not without danger for the closers — if Lapidarist is allowed to coast at its own pace and kicks clear inside the final furlong, no horse in a field of slow-starters can mount a meaningful response. The pace-setter's true running style is prominent rather than pure front-runner, but undisturbed at the head of affairs it may simply prove too far ahead at the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Backmarkers Sprint Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine hold-up horses — King Of The Dance, Prophet Squeeze, City Escape — get a clear run but the race is simply too slowly run for them to overhaul the pace.
scenarios.body: A slow gallop leaves true backmarkers too much to do from their natural position, and those pushed widest and furthest back in a bunched field are first blocked and then outpaced when the sprint begins. This scenario produces a winning margin in favour of prominent racers while the real hold-up horses, City Escape and Prophet Squeeze in particular, finish with running left but too little track remaining.

watchPoints.text: Watch Lapidarist in the opening two furlongs — if she drifts back from the lead rather than controlling the pace, there is no natural replacement and the race could descend into a crawl that produces a dramatically compressed final sprint with no clear tactical winner.

Monitor Typeface and Charencey for position in the early stages — both are capable of racing closer than their hold-up tags and if they take up a pitch just off Lapidarist's shoulder, they become the primary dangers and the race dynamic shifts away from true late-closers entirely.

Gert Lush's jockey Gina Mangan must decide quickly whether to push forward past the hold-up cluster — in a bunched field at a slow pace, being trapped on the inside rail through Ffos Las's bends could cost her a clear run at a crucial stage.

Strong Man Tom's tendency to fade in the finish is acutely relevant today — if the race becomes a sprint from two furlongs out at a fast clip, he is the horse most likely to be pulled up or badly beaten and could become an obstacle for horses trying to find a late run on his outside.

With eleven runners, most of them hold-up types, watch the final bend for crowding — City Escape and King Of The Dance, both natural backmarkers pushed into mid-division, may cause interference if they switch wide for a run simultaneously in the home straight.

races.name: Ascona Ladies Race Day Elegance Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Cogital
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old hold-up type with two wins and four places in similar going, notably won over 17f on good recently suggesting this 1m4f is well within range; Donagh Murphy (7lb claim) helps at the weights and the Bernard Llewellyn yard is 0/7 in the last 14 days, so trainer form is the mild concern.

runners_data.name: Virtual Hug
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a win and two places over 1m2f on good, genuine hold-up racer who will be forced to sit closer to the pace than ideal given the field composition; Nikki Evans sends just one runner here and the 24-day absence is fine, but racing out of position is a real constraint on its chance.

runners_data.name: Buck Barrow
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old with three places on good at 1m2f and a soft-ground win; Adrian Wintle's yard has landed one from five in the last fortnight which is modest, and though its hold-up style is its natural game, the field dynamics push it forward — the step to 1m4f for the first time is the additional unknown.

runners_data.name: Master Dancer
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who carries the headgear flag (visor) and whose recent record shows worrying finishes deep in the field at 1m2f on good; 46 days off since last run is not alarming but the natural late-running style will be compromised by a single front-runner setting a gentle tempo, and the form string is unconvincing.

runners_data.name: Adrian
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has placed at 2m on soft and handles testing conditions well but whose two going runs on good are limited; 78 days since last run is the longest absence in the field, the blinkers are noted, and Bernard Llewellyn's 0/7 recent strike rate adds trainer concern — he will need things to go right from the rear.

runners_data.name: Atalanta Mist
runners_data.note: Consistent three-year-old filly who has placed five times in a row including twice on good ground, and the step from 1m2f to 1m4f looks like it suits a horse that stays on rather than quickens; Jack Doughty takes the ride for Marcus Tregoning who is 1/6 in the last 14 days, and the lighter weight of 127lbs is an advantage in the handicap.

runners_data.name: Saxophonic
runners_data.note: Three-year-old tagged with a fade warning having been beaten a long way out in recent starts; the one placed effort on similar going is encouraging but the trainer David Simcock is 0/8 in the last fortnight and the hold-up style in a race with only one front-runner leaves this horse dependent on a truly run race that is unlikely to materialise.

runners_data.name: Dream Of Ithaca
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race, she broke her maiden over 1m2f on good at this course last time out and should lead comfortably throughout; the step up to 1m4f is untested and the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that she is naturally a prominent racer now being asked to front up alone, but in a field of hold-up types she has a clear positional advantage.

runners_data.name: Emerald Reine
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old filly with just three runs, all on standard-to-slow ground and all finishing in the 7-9 range; the 86-day layoff is the longest in the field and she steps up markedly in trip having not gone beyond 1m1f — Julia & Shelley Birkett are 1/3 in the last 14 days but experience and form are major concerns here.

runners_data.name: Beau Chevalier
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has finished between fifth and twelfth in all five career starts, all on good or good-to-soft at 7f-1m, and carries a fade warning; the step to 1m4f is a significant distance jump with no evidence of staying ability, and Rose Dawes (5lb claim) cannot fully compensate for a horse that has yet to threaten at shorter trips.

races.paceDynamic: Dream Of Ithaca is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 1m4f handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will be able to dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the outset on good ground at Ffos Las. The nine remaining runners are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the pace is likely to be controlled and measured rather than searching, which typically compresses the field and limits the premium on finishing speed. Several nominally midfield-placed runners — Virtual Hug, Buck Barrow, Master Dancer, Adrian, Emerald Reine and Beau Chevalier — are in fact true hold-up horses redistributed forward on the pace map because the rear of the field is overcrowded; in reality, the bulk of the field will be chasing Dream Of Ithaca from varying distances off a single-paced front. This race shape strongly favours Dream Of Ithaca herself and any horse capable of tracking her into the straight and producing a sustained, if modest, finishing effort — a patient prominent or early-to-challenge profile benefits most in a slowly-run, strung-out contest where late closers will struggle to generate meaningful momentum off a steady gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dream Of Ithaca Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Of Ithaca bowls along uncontested and dictates a fair but undemanding pace throughout the 1m4f trip.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to push her, she settles into a rhythm, conserves energy, and simply needs to find enough in the straight to hold on; her recent course win at 1m2f on good shows she handles the conditions and the step up is the one question.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Dream Of Ithaca within two lengths throughout and produces a timely challenge turning for home.
scenarios.body: The controlled pace means the race is not truly run for hold-up types, so a horse sitting second or third and quickening off the bend has the clearest passage; Atalanta Mist's consistent placed record on good ground and Cogital's prior wins at this sort of trip make them the likeliest beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Catch Them
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Of Ithaca goes too fast too soon or the pace is stronger than expected, opening the door for hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: Even in this scenario the redistributed hold-up horses must race wide of their natural position and eat into a comfortable lead — Virtual Hug and Buck Barrow have the finishing form at 1m2f-1m4f on good to make them the most credible threats, though their STYLE_FIT tags temper expectations.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Modest Pace, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so tepid that the entire field bunches turning in and the race becomes a sprint finish for a 10-runner field.
scenarios.body: In a muddling contest form becomes harder to unravel and lower-weighted younger horses who stay on steadily could feature; Emerald Reine and Beau Chevalier are outsiders here but the lack of proven finishing speed and the fade flags against both.

watchPoints.text: Dream Of Ithaca leads uncontested — watch whether Liam Wright (5lb claimer) uses the easy lead to coast or pushes on to set a proper test, as the winning margin of her last run suggests she may hold a genuinely comfortable advantage if allowed to dictate.

Atalanta Mist has placed in five consecutive starts and may sit closest to Dream Of Ithaca in the early stages — if she tracks the leader throughout rather than dropping back into the hold-up pack, she becomes the most dangerous shape-fit challenger turning for home.

Virtual Hug and Buck Barrow are true hold-up horses forced forward by field dynamics — watch if either jockey fights for a position in mid-division early, as being caught three or four wide in an unfamiliar role could cost them ground and momentum in the straight.

Cogital is 52 days since last run for a yard without a recent winner — watch whether Donagh Murphy (7lb claim) tries to position the 11-year-old closer than usual to compensate for the slow pace, as this horse's placed form on good over extended trips makes it dangerous if it can travel near the pace.

Beau Chevalier and Saxophonic both carry official fade flags — if either appears to be going well into the home turn, treat it with caution as neither has demonstrated the ability to sustain an effort at this trip or beyond.
